newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Singapore air pact includes cargo services.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Singapore air pact includes cargo services.

text.p: The United States and Singapore have reached an "open skies" aviation agreement to end curbs on passenger and cargo services between the two countries, the Transportation Department said on Thursday.
It said the pact, negotiated the past two days and initialed Thursday, will allow airlines of both countries to fly without restrictions to and beyond each other's countries.

The department added that the accord broke new ground beyond "open skies" pacts reached with 12 European nations by giving Singapore and U.S. carriers the right to operate cargo hubs in the other's countries.
The department said these rights allow U.S. airlines to fly cargo from Singapore to throughtout Asia.
U.S. carriers serving Singapore are United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp., and Northwest Airlines Corp.
The United States is served by Singapore Airlines.
"This agreement initiates what we hope will be a series of open skies relationships with our partners in Asia," Transportation Secretary Federico Pena said in a statement.

He said it is part of President Clinton's goal of open aviation markets worldwide, with the promise of benefits for passengers and shippers in terms of better and more frequent services and lower fares.
The department said "open skies" talks would be held next month with Malaysia and Taiwan, and hoped that in the near future talks could be held with South Korea and New Zealand.
Discussions with Brunei are being held now, it added.
